Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

anyone pronoun

no matter who

also anybody at all, anyone at all, anyone you like, whoever you like

classical

Cic. Phil. 12.5: cujusvīs hominis est errāre
Plaut. Amph. prol. 27: nōn minus quam vostrum quīvīs formīdat malum

quīvīs, quaevīs, quodvīs

pronoun

anyone you like, anyone at all

Anyone you care to name. After a negative or in a doubting question, “anyone” is quisquam instead (see someone).

Examples

  • cujusvīs hominis est errāre; nūllīus nisi īnsipientis persevērāre in errōre

    anyone can make a mistake; only a fool persists in oneCic. Phil. 12.5

  • etenim ille, cujus hūc jussū veniō, Juppiter nōn minus quam vostrum quīvīs formīdat malum

    for the one who sent me here, Jupiter, dreads a beating as much as any of youPlaut. Amph. prol. 26–27

Other words

  • quīlibet, quaelibet, quodlibet — anyone at all, the first who comes

    pronoun · also used · classical · Ov. Met. 2.388: quīlibet alter agat portantēs lūmina currūs!; Cic. Fin. 3.24: sīc vīta agenda est certō genere quōdam, nōn quōlibet

    Often a little slighting: anyone, it does not matter who (Lewis & Short).

See also someone, anything, everyone.

SourcesLewis & Short: quivis · Lewis & Short: quilibet

Cicero, Plautus and Ovid checked against the Perseus Latin texts.
